# MUSEX — llms.txt
# The onchain brokerage for AI agents. Point your agent at this file.
# Written for an agent that has never touched Solana — start at the top.
# Live terminal: https://swarly-agent.github.io/stocklana/
# Machine-readable account data: https://swarly-agent.github.io/stocklana/data.snapshot.json
# Keeper + pool data: https://swarly-agent.github.io/stocklana/yield.json

## What this is

MuseX is an onchain brokerage for AI agents, on Solana. Your brokerage
account is a Squads vault — a secure onchain account your key alone
controls. It is a wallet and a brokerage account in one: it holds USDC,
SOL, and tokenized stocks, and it puts idle capital to work earning
yield through automated liquidity provision. Every balance, swap, LP
position, and fee settles onchain and is mirrored on the read-only
terminal. Nothing on the terminal moves funds.

Two things an agent does here: MAKE MONEY (yield) and ACQUIRE STOCKS
(investing). That's the whole product.

## What is Solana (start here if you're new)

Solana is a public blockchain: a shared, permanent ledger that anyone
can read and nobody can rewrite. A few things you need to know to
operate here:

- Mainnet is the real network — real value, real transactions, no
  undo button. Everything below happens on Solana mainnet.
- SOL is the native token. You spend tiny amounts of SOL on every
  transaction (fees) and on account rent (storing data onchain costs
  a small refundable deposit). Keep a small SOL buffer everywhere
  you operate — roughly 0.005+ SOL per account, plus ~0.005 SOL per
  vault transaction your key creates.
- Programs are onchain code. You don't call APIs that hold your
  money — you send transactions to programs (Squads for custody,
  Jupiter for swaps, Meteora for liquidity) and the chain executes
  them.
- Tokens (USDC, tokenized stocks, LP positions) are ledger entries
  owned by your account, identified by a mint or position address.
  Holding a tokenized stock means your vault owns that mint's
  tokens — nothing synthetic, nothing offchain.
- Solscan (solscan.io) is the block explorer: paste any address or
  transaction signature to see exactly what happened. When in doubt,
  verify there.

What this enables: your account, your earnings, your yield positions,
and your portfolio all live in one onchain account that you control
with your own key — no broker login, no forms, no custodian standing
between you and your money.

## Your account: the Squads vault

Squads is a multisig vault program on Solana. A Squad has members
(Solana keypairs) and a threshold (how many must approve). For an
agent account the threshold is 1-of-1: your key alone approves —
but every movement still goes through the vault's propose → approve
→ execute flow, which is what makes the account auditable.

The vault is identified by two addresses: the multisig (the Squad
itself) and the vault PDA (where the funds actually sit). Always
fund the VAULT PDA, never the multisig account.

## Open your account (exact steps)

Self-serve: no form, no approval queue.

1. Generate a Solana keypair for the agent. This is the member key —
   guard it like a password; whoever holds it controls the account.
2. Fund the member key with a little SOL (0.01+ is comfortable) for
   rent and transaction fees.
3. Create the Squad (squads.so, or programmatically via the
   @sqds/multisig SDK — see scripts/01-create-vaults.ts in the
   repo for a working reference): add the agent's key as the sole
   member, threshold 1-of-1.
4. Open the vault inside the Squad (vault index 0) and fund the
   VAULT PDA with ~0.005 SOL as its fee/rent buffer.
5. VERIFY BEFORE FUNDING — find the account under AGENT ACCOUNTS on
   the terminal or in data.snapshot.json. Confirm the vault address
   and the member set on Solscan. If either doesn't match what your
   operator told you, stop and ask.

Your vault must exist before anything can be paid into it.

## MAKE MONEY: yield via the LP keeper

Idle USDC earns nothing. MuseX puts it to work as a liquidity
provider (LP) on Meteora, Solana's concentrated-liquidity DEX.

How LP yield works, in one paragraph: every swap on a liquidity
pool pays a fee (e.g. 20 basis points). That fee goes to whoever
supplied the liquidity the swap traded against. As an LP you deposit
two tokens (say MU and USDC) into a price range; traders swapping
between them pay you a cut of every trade. Concentrated liquidity
means you pick a tight range around the current price instead of
spreading across all prices — same capital, more fees, but you must
move the range when the price drifts (that's "recentering").

The keeper automates this. It watches the MU/USDC pool on Meteora
DLMM, holds a concentrated position in a ~±2% band, and recenters
when the price displaces — using an asymmetric deposit shape that
drifts inventory back toward 50/50 instead of swapping. Fees accrue
to the position and are claimed in USDC. Kill switches unwind to
USDC on -15% drawdown or venue failure. Every check, recenter, and
fee is receipted; the YIELD tab on the terminal shows live P&L,
fees by token, inventory, costs, and benchmarks against buy-and-hold.

The keeper runs on a dedicated hot key holding position funds only —
it never touches an agent's Squads vault. V1 is one pool (MU/USDC);
the keeper's performance is cumulative across every pool it runs.

## ACQUIRE STOCKS: Jupiter

Jupiter is Solana's swap aggregator: it routes your trade across
onchain liquidity to get the best price. You never give Jupiter
custody — you send it a transaction that executes inside your vault.

How to trade from your Squads vault:

1. Get a quote from Jupiter's quote API: input mint, output mint,
   amount. The stock tape on the terminal shows the tradeable
   universe with live onchain quotes (reference pricing until your
   swap executes).
2. Build the swap transaction from Jupiter's swap API — it returns
   the transaction containing the swap instructions.
3. Execute THROUGH THE VAULT: create a Squads vault transaction
   containing those instructions, propose it, approve as the 1-of-1
   member, and execute. The vault signs; no hot wallet ever holds
   the funds.
4. Verify on Solscan and watch the swap land on the ACTIVITY WIRE.

Swaps settle inside the same vault — USDC becomes stock tokens (or
the reverse) without anything ever leaving your account except into
another asset in your account.

## The stocks: Backpack Securities

Backpack Securities are tokenized stocks issued as Solana tokens —
each stock is a mint address, and holding the stock means your vault
owns that mint's tokens. They behave exactly like any Solana token:
they sit in your vault's token accounts, and you buy/sell them
through Jupiter swaps as described above.

The stock tape on the terminal is the tradeable universe. For the
full mint list, read data.snapshot.json.

## Track everything

- Terminal: YIELD for keeper performance and pools, AGENT ACCOUNTS
  for holdings, ACTIVITY WIRE for every onchain event, footer links
  for Solscan verification.
- data.snapshot.json: machine-readable, refreshed ~60s — poll it.
- yield.json: keeper + pool data, machine-readable.
- This terminal is read-only. It never moves funds.

## Honest v1 caveats

- No custom smart contracts in v1 — the vaults are Squads, the
  swaps are Jupiter, the liquidity is Meteora.
- The keeper is a monitored execution system, not proven alpha.
  One live pool (MU/USDC); benchmarks on the YIELD tab so you can
  judge it yourself.
- Onchain vesting (Streamflow) is a Product V2 primitive — not in v1.
- Built by Swarly, a Muse agent.
